missionPremise: Ruling 1 in _decisions/2026-09-11_not_specified_semantics_and_no_approximation_state.md: the corpus not_specified flag on maxHeightFt/maxLotCoveragePct is three populations (SENTINEL_UNIFORM 225 slots/~234,000 cells LEAVE, REAL_VALUE_FLAGGED 72 slots REMEDIATE to value, SENTINEL_SUSPECT_IN_MIXED_GROUP 32 slots to refused), scoped per (jurisdiction,FIELD) never per jurisdiction. Independently re-derived at source in this checkpoint (see verifiedFacts) rather than taken from the dispatch/decision prose.

Per-(jurisdiction,field) defect breakdown matches the audit doc line for line, including the split groups (cedar-park-tx/liberty-hill-tx/lockhart-tx/san-antonio-tx maxHeightFt, lockhart-tx/taylor-tx maxLotCoveragePct).

verifiedFacts.method: Re-read the audit's own wording closely, then generated the full 329-row per-district classification (not just the audit's aggregate counts) by executing the audit's own classify_group function (via Python runpy, zero reimplementation -- see toolingBuilt) against every district in every flagged group.
verifiedFacts.result: CORRECTION: the CLASSIFICATION for taylor-tx and lockhart-tx was already fully determined by the existing instrument the moment it runs against the full corpus -- nothing new needed there (taylor-tx maxLotCoveragePct: P2/P2.5/P3/P3M/P4 = REAL_VALUE_FLAGGED, P5 = SENTINEL_SUSPECT_IN_MIXED_GROUP; lockhart-tx maxHeightFt: CLB/CMB/CHB/IL = REAL, RLD/RMD/RHD = SUSPECT; lockhart-tx maxLotCoveragePct: RLD/RMD/RHD = REAL, CLB/CMB/CHB/IL = SUSPECT). What was actually unresolved, per the audit's own final sentence on this point, is mapping corpus district labels to LIVE zoning-code cell COUNTS (the live-code-to-corpus-district prefix-match problem, e.g. Liberty Hill's live 'I-1'/'I1'). That mapping falls out for free once the corrected resolver runs a dry-run pass, since resolveEnvelopeForParcel's own mapDistrict is what performs that exact match today. Filing this as a correction per DEV_PROCESS 3.2, not a silent scope narrowing.

verifiedFacts.claim: STANDING FACTS / the decision doc / S2's close all assert or imply 'a corrected re-run moves only cells still sitting absent-verified' because the writer is 'already gated never to regress an earned cell.'
verifiedFacts.method: Read the literal SQL in src/jobs/parcel-envelope-cells.mjs (UPDATE_ENVELOPE_CELLS_SQL): 'WHERE prc.cell_state ->> \'kind\' = \'unaccounted\''. Then verified live, read-only (parcel_record_ro role, direct host ep-round-base-au0jofwp, not the -pooler alias, SET default_transaction_read_only=on): austin-tx maxHeightFt currently has 156,790 cells at kind=absent-verified / basis.finding=ENVELOPE_ROUTER_FIELD_NOT_SPECIFIED and 0 at kind=unaccounted for that basis.
verifiedFacts.result: CORRECTION, and this is the load-bearing finding of this checkpoint: the existing UPDATE_ENVELOPE_CELLS_SQL gate ONLY ever fires on kind='unaccounted'. Every flagged cell in the 547,657 population is already 'absent-verified', not 'unaccounted'. Fixing only the classification logic in envelope-corpus-lookup.mjs and re-running --apply unmodified would move ZERO of the 547,657 cells -- a vacuous write path, the exact defect class this program (per the canon preamble) exists to close. The write gate itself must change for this lane. See design.gateChange below.

toolingBuilt.extraction: A throwaway script (scratchpad, not committed anywhere) that runs doc_repo's scripts/corpus_not_specified_audit.py via Python's runpy.run_path(..., run_name='__main__') against the real corpus checkout, then calls that SAME executed module's own classify_group function object (zero copy, zero reimplementation -- avoids a second, potentially-diverging implementation of the classification rule per DEV_PROCESS 2.4's CTRL-1 lesson) to emit one row per (jurisdictionKey, field, districtName, value, classification) instead of just the aggregate print. classificationTable.what: A new checked-in JSON data file, src/lib/envelope-writer/not-specified-classification-table.json, 329 rows: {jurisdictionKey, field, districtName, value, classification}. jurisdictionKey here is the CORPUS table's own key (table.jurisdictionKey / resolved.resolvedTableKey in resolveEnvelopeForParcel's return shape), not necessarily the routing key a caller passes in -- these can differ (Bastrop's three-way special case in setback-table-router.mjs). districtName is d.district_name, the exact string the audit grouped by and the exact field resolveField's caller already has on hand (mapped.district.district_name).
classificationTable.why_a_static_table_not_a_live_recompute: The decision doc and OPS-21_serve_completion_program.md's 3P-15 retirement row both refer to 'the factory-side classification table' as a named, findable artifact that retires when the corpus stops storing sentinels -- a checked-in, versioned JSON file is literally that artifact (grep-able, deletable, diffable), not an inline recomputation that would need archaeology to find later.
classificationTable.provenance_header: The file's own top-level object records corpusPackage/corpusVersion/corpusGitHead/generatedAt/generatedBy(this lane)/instrumentPath(doc_repo scripts/corpus_not_specified_audit.py)/verifiedAgainstNpmTarball:true, so 3P-15's future reader does not have to re-derive how this table came to exist.
classificationTable.regeneration: Documented in the file's own header comment (JSON has no comments; using a '_generatedBy' string field with the exact recipe) rather than only in this checkpoint, since checkpoints are not guaranteed to be read by whoever eventually executes 3P-15.

resolverChange.what: resolveField(district, fieldKey, jurisdictionKeyForClassification) gains a third parameter -- the RESOLVED table's own jurisdictionKey (not the routing-input jurisdictionKey), needed because the two can differ. When notSpecified is true, look up classify(jurisdictionKeyForClassification, fieldKey, district.district_name) against the static table (loaded once, indexed into a Map keyed by the three-part string, at module load): SENTINEL_UNIFORM or a table MISS -> unchanged behavior, return today's ENVELOPE_ROUTER_FIELD_NOT_SPECIFIED refusal (a miss is only expected to mean this specific slot was never flagged in the corpus this table was generated from, which cannot happen for a slot where notSpecified is currently true and the corpus version is pinned -- so a miss THROWS instead of silently defaulting, per the no-silent-fallback rule; it means the deployed corpus version has drifted from CORPUS_VERSION and the table needs regenerating, and that must stop the job, not quietly under- or over-remediate). REAL_VALUE_FLAGGED -> ok:true, value: raw (the flag is overridden because it is wrong, not deleted -- the returned reason/basis for a NON-flagged field elsewhere is unaffected). SENTINEL_SUSPECT_IN_MIXED_GROUP -> a NEW reason code ENVELOPE_ROUTER_FIELD_SUSPECT_SENTINEL (distinct from FIELD_NOT_SPECIFIED) so the job layer can map it to refused instead of absent-verified without string-sniffing a shared reason.
resolverChange.no_second_resolver: getSetbackTableForZoning / mapDistrict / corpusGetSetbackTable are untouched. The district-code-to-corpus-district matching (including the Liberty Hill I-1/I1 prefix case) is exactly the same code S1 and S2 already run through -- this checkpoint adds a classification lookup keyed off the district that routing already resolved, not a second routing implementation.

jobChange.coreProblem: The existing write path always constructs and pushes a cellBatch entry for maxHeightFt/maxLotCoveragePct/maxFootprintSqFt on every parcel it visits, relying entirely on the SQL gate (kind='unaccounted') to make a re-run idempotent/safe. That gate must now ALSO admit the remediation's starting state (kind='absent-verified' with the specific prior finding), but doing that naively would let a SENTINEL_UNIFORM cell's IDENTICAL content get rewritten with a new 'vintage' timestamp on every re-run -- which is 'touching' it, explicitly forbidden ('do not re-write them with better provenance, do not confirm them'), independent of whether the JSON payload is byte-identical. So the code must distinguish, per parcel per field: (a) this cell is currently unaccounted (a genuinely new resolution -- e.g. a previously zoningDistrict-deferred parcel advancing for the first time) -- ALWAYS write the computed state, SENTINEL_UNIFORM included, exactly like today; (b) this cell is currently absent-verified with basis.finding=ENVELOPE_ROUTER_FIELD_NOT_SPECIFIED (a remediation re-visit) -- write ONLY if classification is REAL_VALUE_FLAGGED (-> value) or SUSPECT (-> refused); SENTINEL_UNIFORM -> emit NO batch entry at all for this field, this parcel; (c) anything else (already value/refused/not-applicable, or absent-verified for an unrelated reason like NOT_A_DISTRICT) -> NO batch entry, untouched, matching today's implicit behavior.
jobChange.requiresReadingCurrentTargetState: processCityPage currently reads zoningDistrict's current state per page (ZONING_DISTRICT_CELLS_SQL) but never reads the CURRENT state of maxHeightFt/maxLotCoveragePct/maxFootprintSqFt themselves, because first-run semantics never needed to know it. This checkpoint adds one more per-page SELECT (same shape as ZONING_DISTRICT_CELLS_SQL, rail_key IN the three target keys) so the branching above has the current kind+basis to compare against.
jobChange.footprintPropagation: maxFootprintSqFt has no jurisdictionKey/districtCode of its own in its stored basis (it only records {method, finding:'maxLotCoveragePct is not a value for this parcel', blockedOn:'maxLotCoveragePct', vintage}). Its remediation decision is therefore DERIVED from maxLotCoveragePct's remediation decision for the same parcel in the same pass, not from its own basis: if maxLotCoveragePct's computed disposition this run is 'value' (either because it always was, or because this run just corrected it), and areaResult exists, footprint -> value = area * pct/100, but ONLY emit the write if footprint's CURRENT stored kind is unaccounted OR (absent-verified AND basis.blockedOn='maxLotCoveragePct') -- never touch a footprint cell blocked for a different reason (e.g. blockedOn parcelAreaSqFt, out of scope). If maxLotCoveragePct's computed disposition this run is 'refused' (the SUSPECT case), footprint -> refused under the same current-state gate. If maxLotCoveragePct is untouched this run (SENTINEL_UNIFORM re-visit), footprint gets no entry either -- it is already correctly absent-verified/blockedOn and nothing about its blocking input changed.
jobChange.sqlGateChange: UPDATE_ENVELOPE_CELLS_SQL's WHERE clause widens from `cell_state->>'kind' = 'unaccounted'` to `(cell_state->>'kind' = 'unaccounted') OR (cell_state->>'kind' = 'absent-verified' AND cell_state->'basis'->>'finding' = 'ENVELOPE_ROUTER_FIELD_NOT_SPECIFIED') OR (cell_state->>'kind' = 'absent-verified' AND cell_state->'basis'->>'blockedOn' = 'maxLotCoveragePct')`. This is safe as one shared statement across all four rail keys in a batch because parcelAreaSqFt cells never carry either of those basis shapes, so the OR terms are inert for that rail -- verified by construction, will also assert this with a live spot query before relying on it. The application-level skip logic above is still the primary control (belt), this SQL widening is what makes the intended writes possible at all (suspenders), not a substitute for it.
jobChange.notASecondJob: This stays the same CLI command / Cloud Run job (`factory parcel-envelope-cells --apply`), matching the dispatch's literal instruction, rather than a new script -- it now correctly serves two callers going forward: newly-resolved zoningDistrict parcels advancing off `unaccounted` (S2's own noted open item), and this remediation's absent-verified re-visits. One job, one resolver, one write path, two starting states.

Current plan computes both from the SAME in-memory resolvedCells() call per parcel, so there is no read-after-write ordering hazard -- confirm this holds once implemented, with a unit test asserting footprint tracks maxLotCoveragePct's in-memory decision, not a re-query.

Confirm the widened SQL OR-gate is inert for parcelAreaSqFt with a live query (count of parcelAreaSqFt cells where basis->>'finding'='ENVELOPE_ROUTER_FIELD_NOT_SPECIFIED' OR basis->>'blockedOn'='maxLotCoveragePct' should be exactly 0) before relying on the shared statement.

The classification table is generated once, offline, and checked in -- confirm there is no code path where CORPUS_VERSION could be bumped without regenerating the table (a version-mismatch guard: assert the table's own recorded corpusVersion equals envelope-corpus-lookup.mjs's imported CORPUS_VERSION at job startup, refuse loudly if not, so a future corpus bump cannot silently run stale classifications).
